As part of FCREPO-1312, an RdfContext enum was introduced in order to specify the kinds of RDF generation that a kernel implementation must support and decouple the HTTP layers from the ModeShape implementation. In particular, the FedoraResource::getTriples method now accepts values from this RdfContext enum. While this works, it prevents extending the existing set of RdfContexts.
Instead of having FedoraResource::getTriples accept one or more enum values, it should use a system of interfaces, which would make it possible to extend the set of RDF generation contexts.

comments.body: This is very good, and in my opinion it would be even better if there were no MINIMAL element in this enum. That will clearly depend on what sort of response should be associated with a Prefer: return=minimal request: whether it should contain triples or not, and if so, which triples.

Yeah, I agree. I don't feel like we've gotten closure on the discussion of what minimal is, tho'. Did we? I know we had a long conversation with Esmé Cowles and Benjamin Armintor about that, and everyone liked Esmé Cowles's design, which I think was return=minimal means no triples, but the absence of Prefer means "return an URI", but I can't remember the details. Any help?

For creates, we are returning no triples with a return=minimal, returning the URI of the created resource by default, and returning the RDF for the resource with return=representation (see https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/34b50e13f249a575d2b0fa23788e11d120ebd45e). But we didn't talk about how that translates to GETs. Does return=minimal mean return nothing when you're doing a GET? Isn't that just a HEAD then?
Yeah, I'm not sure how that makes sense. I think Prefer=minimal for GET is maybe just "omit server-managed"? Or maybe it's a certain subset of triples? See FCREPO-1929 Closed .
